title: Lali (log drum pair)
summary: The lali is a pair of hollowed logs of Fiji, one large and one small, each with a long narrow slit. Laid side by side and struck with two long beaters, the thick lips give deep strokes and the thin lips bright ones, and the two logs answer each other.
howToPlay: The two logs lie on a woven mat seen from above: the large one at the top, the small one below it.
Each log has a thick lip for a low tone and a thin lip for a higher tone. Big low and Big high are on the large log, Small low and Small high on the small one.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the big log alone, then bring in the small log.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: In Fijian villages the lali is beaten to call people together and to mark the start of a gathering. Players learn to make the large and small logs speak in turn, so a short pattern can be heard from one end of the village to the other.
credits: Tradition: the Lali; patterns written for this game
